title: Convert Your Hourly Rate to an Annual hr Salary: A Guide for Australian Workers
description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to an annual hr salary using the 38-hour week. Includes national minimum wage, casual loading, super, and tax estimates for 2026-27.
salarySummary: Based on a 38-hour week, the national minimum wage of $26.44 per hour equals an annual gross salary of $52,254.80 before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the current national minimum wage in Australia?
faqs.a: From 1 July 2026, the national minimum wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour. These rates are set by the Fair Work Commission.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard 38-hour week, annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, $30 per hour × 38 × 52 = $59,280 per year. Remember that superannuation is paid on top of this amount.

faqs.q: Does my superannuation count as part of my salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation guarantee contributions are paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings, currently at 12% of your ordinary time earnings up to the maximum contribution base ($270,830 for 2026-27). It is not deducted from your salary but is an additional benefit. Your total remuneration package includes both your salary and super.

bodyMarkdown:
## Introduction

When you're evaluating a job offer or planning your budget, converting your hourly rate to an annual hr salary gives you a clearer picture of your total earnings. In Australia, the standard full-time week is 38 hours, and your pay may include casual loading, penalty rates, and superannuation on top. This guide uses the latest official figures from the Fair Work Commission and the Australian Taxation Office to help you make accurate calculations.

## The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the national minimum wage each year. From 1 July 2026, the rate is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 ordinary hours. This is the minimum for adult employees not covered by an award or agreement. However, most workers are covered by an industry or occupation award, which often has higher minimum rates. For example, the Social, Community, Home Care and Disability Services Award (SCHADS) has specific rates for home care employees, with increases scheduled from December 2026. You can find the correct award for your job using the Fair Work Ombudsman's pay guides. The Fair Work Ombudsman also provides a Pay Calculator to check your minimum entitlements.

### Special Minimum Wages

The National Minimum Wage Order also sets special rates for juniors, apprentices, trainees, and employees with a disability. For example, junior employees under 21 receive a percentage of the adult rate based on age. Apprentices and trainees have rates linked to the Miscellaneous Award 2020. These special rates ensure fair pay for all workers.

## Casual Loading Explained

Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave such as annual leave and sick leave. For the national minimum wage, that means $33.05 per hour. When you use our [the timesheet](/) to calculate your annual hr salary, you can check a box to add casual loading. Never enter a rate that already includes loading; the tool adds it for you. This loading applies to all casual employees, whether award-covered or award-free.

## Superannuation Paid on Top

Your employer must pay superannuation guarantee contributions at 12% of your ordinary time earnings, on top of your salary. This means if your annual gross salary is $60,000, your employer contributes an additional $7,200 to your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 (2026-27). Super is not deducted from your pay; it's an extra benefit that boosts your total remuneration. For more details, see our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page. Note that the super guarantee rate is scheduled to increase to 12.5% from 1 July 2028.

## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Salary

The basic formula is: annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For a standard 38-hour week, that's hourly × 38 × 52. For example:

- $26.44/hour × 38 × 52 = $52,254.80 per year (national minimum wage)
- $33.05/hour (casual) × 38 × 52 = $65,318.80 per year
- $40/hour × 38 × 52 = $79,040 per year
- $50/hour × 38 × 52 = $98,800 per year

If you work part-time or irregular hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. Our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page has more examples and a table of common rates.

## Fortnightly Pay and Weekly Breakdown

Many employers pay fortnightly. Your fortnightly gross pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two. For the minimum wage, weekly is $1,004.90, so fortnightly is $2,009.80 before tax. Casual workers at $33.05/hour earn $1,255.90 per week, or $2,511.80 per fortnight. Knowing your fortnightly amount helps with budgeting, especially if you're paid on that cycle.

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

The Australian Taxation Office applies progressive tax rates for 2026-27: nil on the first $18,200, 15% on income up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. Most residents also pay a 2% Medicare levy. For example, on a $65,318.80 annual salary (casual minimum wage), the tax would be approximately $9,967 (using the 2026-27 rates) plus Medicare levy of $1,306, leaving a take-home of about $54,045. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool to estimate your net pay after tax and Medicare. Note that the calculator does not deduct HELP repayments, Medicare levy surcharge, or salary sacrifice amounts.

## Using the Timesheet

Our [the timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and see the annual, weekly, fortnightly, and monthly figures. It also estimates tax and super. Remember, the calculator assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For award-specific rates, check the [pay guides](/blog) or [reference tables](/data). The timesheet is designed for quick estimates; for precise payroll calculations, consult your employer or a tax professional.

## Average Weekly Earnings for Context

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports average weekly earnings. In May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week, which equates to an annual salary of about $108,352. All employees total earnings (including part-time) averaged $1,579.20 per week, or $82,118 annually. These figures give you a benchmark for where your hr salary sits in the broader market.

## Conclusion

Understanding your hr salary in annual terms helps you compare offers and plan your finances. Always consider casual loading, super, and tax. For the most accurate figures, refer to the Fair Work Ombudsman and the Australian Taxation Office. Use our tools to get a quick estimate, and remember that your total remuneration package includes super on top.
